text:
maria.g: FYI alert — NAT ephemeral ports saturated in us-west-2 edge fleet, starting ~12:12 UTC. infra alarm: \"ephemeral_ports_used=65535/65535\". Customer-facing model pulls returning 502/connection_reset.

devin: Saw the spike on Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/board/d/Egress/egress-ports?orgId=1&var-region=us-west-2 — huge fanout from model-fetch jobs at 12:10.

raj.k: Quick check: conntrack count is pegged. Ran `ss -s` on an affected node, lots of TIME_WAIT and ephemeral allocations. Snippet:
```
Total: 65535 (kernel 0)
TCP:   30000 established, 20000 timewait, 15000 syn-recv
```

ethan.s: Are these image/model pulls hitting dockerhub or S3? If it's registry.docker.io we're getting tons of short-lived TCP connects.

maria.g: Confirmed many pulls from registry mirror + S3 presigned fetches for shard artifacts. Two immediate impacts: 1) model-load latency spikes, 2) egress retries amplify port churn.

sre_oncall: What do we want as the hotfix? Options: add NAT gateways, deploy NAT instances, route pulls through an egress proxy with keepalive, or throttle concurrent pulls at the runtime.

devin: Adding NAT gateways is fastest to lower immediate error rate but costs jump. Root cause is connection churn from parallel fetches + no connection reuse. Short term: scale NAT capacity + enable an egress proxy. Medium: change runtime to reuse HTTP/2 or keepalive connections + reduce parallelism for downloads.

raj.k: Tactical runbook I propose:
- 12:25 create 2 extra NAT gateways in the AZs with higher port ranges (request in console).
- 12:30 roll out envoy egress proxy as DaemonSet with HTTP/2 mux for model pulls to a small canary subset (100 nodes).
- 12:45 patch ai-runtime image loader to limit concurrent downloads to 4 per node and enable persistent connections.

maria.g: I'll submit the NAT create request now and start the envoy canary.

infra-bot: [auto] NATGateway create request submitted: req-0a1b2c3d in us-west-2 (creating 2x gateways). ETA ~ 4 min.

deploy-bot: [auto] Canaries: envoy-egress/daemonset rollout started -> 25/100 nodes updated.

ethan.s: Also recommend immediate config changes:
- Ensure imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent on model pods.
- Add pod-level throttle annotation for runtime: `redwood.io/max-parallel-fetches: \"4\"`.
- Enable VPC S3 endpoint for artifact buckets so S3 fetches don't use NAT.

devin: Agree on S3 VPC endpoints — that will cut a large portion of egress. Also file to migrate large artifacts to a private ECR mirror (less external DNS / connection churn).

maria.g: Status check 12:40 — NAT create succeeded, new gateways attached to route table. Observed drop in port saturation immediately (ephemeral_ports_used ~ 32000/65535). 502s down from 18% to 4%.

sre_oncall: Good. Next: schedule runtime change for persistent HTTP and limit concurrency. Who owns the runtime patch?

raj.k: I'll take the runtime patch. Will open PR for connection pooling + a flag to limit parallel downloads. Target canary tomorrow AM.

devin: I'll own the infra follow-up: request formal capacity increase plan or autoscaling for NATs, and work with finance on cost estimate.

maria.g: Action items:
- raj.k: runtime patch + canary (owner)
- devin: long-term NAT autoscaling plan + ECR mirror work (owner)
- ops: continue envoy canary and expand if metrics keep improving

infra-bot: [auto] Metric snapshot saved: egress_ports_us-west-2_2026-03-18T12:45Z -> saved to /metrics/snapshots/2323456789.json

maria.g: Closing loop — temporary mitigation worked, still treating this as P2 until runtime fixes and S3/ECR migration reduce external connection blast. We'll reconvene after runtime canary. :thumbsup:
